questions.q: If the co-efficient of $x^{7}$ and $x^{8}$ in the expansion of~\left(2 + \dfrac{x}{3}\right)n$ are equal, then the value of $n$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have, the co-efficient of $x^{7}$ and $x^{8}$ in the expansion of~\left(2 + \dfrac{x}{3}\right)n$ are equal.

Therefore,~$C7 n {2}^{n - 7}\dfrac{1}{37} = C8 n {2}^{n - 8}\dfrac{1}{38}$

$⇒ n - 7 = 48$

$⇒ n = 55 .$

$

questions.q: The remainder on dividing ${5}^{99}$ by $11$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Now to divide& ${5}^{99}$~by~$11$~we need to check the cyclicity of power of~$5$~when divided by~$11$,

So remainder when~$\dfrac{51}{11} \to 5\text{as remainder}$

Similarly,

$\dfrac{52}{11} = \dfrac{25}{11} \to 3\text{as remainder}$

$\dfrac{53}{11} = \dfrac{125}{11} \to 4\text{as remainder}$

$\dfrac{54}{11} = \dfrac{625}{11} \to 9\text{as remainder}$

And~$\dfrac{55}{11} = \dfrac{3125}{11} \to 1\text{as remainder}$

So, rewriting the expression we get,~\left({5}^{5}\right)19 \times {5}^{4}$

Now when~$\dfrac{\left({5}^{5}\right)19 \times {5}^{4}}{11} \to 1 \times \dfrac{54}{11}$

Now again simplifying we get,~$\dfrac{54}{11} \to 9\text{as remainder}$.

$

questions.q: The coefficient of& $x^{7}$~in~\left(1 - x + 2x^{3}\right)10$ \text{ and } is __________ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We need to find the coefficient of& $x^{7}$~in~\left(1 - x + 2x^{3}\right)10$.

We know that for~\left(x + y + z\right)n$,~

${T}_{n} = \dfrac{n !}{a ! b ! c !}\left(x\right)a\left(y\right)b\left(z\right)c$~such that~$a + b + c = n$

Now for~\left(1 - x + 2x^{3}\right)10$

${T}_{n} = \dfrac{10 !}{a ! b ! c !}\left(1\right)a\left(- x\right)b\left(2x^{3}\right)c$

$= \dfrac{10 !}{a ! b ! c !}\left(- 1\right)b{2}^{c}x^{b + 3c}$. with~$a + b + c = 10$

Here we need coefficient of~$x^{7}$.

Hence the combinations would be

$\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ 3 & 7 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 7 & 1 & 2\end{cases}$~

which satisfies both~$a + b + c = 10$~and~$b + 3c = 7$.

Hence, coefficient of~$x^{7}$~will be,

~$= \dfrac{10 !}{2 ! 1 ! 7 !}\left(2\right)2\left(- 1\right)1$

$+ \dfrac{10 !}{1 ! 4 ! 5 !}\left(2\right)1\left(- 1\right)4 + \dfrac{10 !}{0 ! 7 ! 3 !}\left(2\right)0\left(- 1\right)7$

$= 960$

$

questions.q: If the maximum value of the term independent of $t$ in the expansion of \left(t^{2}x\dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{\left(1 - x\right)\dfrac{1}{10}}{t}\right)15, x \ge 0$, is $K$, then $8K$ is equal to _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(t^{2}x\dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{\left(1 - x\right)\dfrac{1}{10}}{t}\right)15$

Now~$r^{th}$~term is given by,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 15 \left(t^{2}x\dfrac{1}{5}\right)15 - r \cdot \dfrac{\left(1 - x\right)\dfrac{r}{10}}{tr}$

For independent of $t$,

$2\left(15 - r\right) - r = 0$

$30 - 2r - r = 0$

$⇒ r = 10$

So, Maximum value of $C10 15 x \left(1 - x\right)$~will be at~$x = $\dfrac{1}{2} \left(\text{as}\dfrac{dy}{dx} \left($x - x^{2}\right) = 1 -2 x & 1 - 2x = 0 ⇒ x = $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$= C10 15 $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3003}{4}

So,~$K = $\dfrac{3003}{4}~and~$8K = 6006$

$

questions.q: Remainder when ${64}^{3232}$ is divided by $9$ is equal to _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${64}^{3232} = \left(63 + 1\right)32 \times 32 \times 32 . . . . 32\text{times}$

$⇒ {64}^{3232} = \left(63 + 1\right)32\lambda$

Now we know that by binomial theorem,

\left(1 + 63\right)32\lambda = C0 {}^{32\lambda} \cdot 1 + C1 {}^{32\lambda} \cdot 1 \cdot 63 + C2 {}^{32\lambda} \cdot 1 \cdot {63}^{2} + . . . . . . .$

$⇒ \left(1 + 63\right)32\lambda = 1 + 9\alpha$

So, when ${64}^{3232}$ is divided by $9$ we get $1$ as remainder.

$

General term $\dfrac{10 !}{\alpha ! \beta ! \gamma !}x^{\beta + 2\gamma}$
For coefficient of $x^{4} ⇒ \beta + 2\gamma = 4$

$\gamma = 1, \beta = 2, \alpha = 7 ⇒ \dfrac{10 !}{7 ! 2 ! 1 !} = 360$
$\gamma = 2, \beta = 0, \alpha = 8 ⇒ \dfrac{10 !}{8 ! 0 ! 2 !} = 45$
Total $= 615$

questions.q:
The constant term in the expansion of
${\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{x^{7}} + 3x^{2}\right)}^{5}$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Any term in the expansion of ${\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{x^{7}} + 3x^{2}\right)}^{5}$ is given by

$\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}{\left(2x\right)}^{a}{\left(x^{- 7}\right)}^{b}{\left(3x^{2}\right)}^{c}$

where $a + b + c = 5 . . . \left(i\right)$

$= {2}^{a}{\left(3\right)}^{c}\left(\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}\right)x^{a}x^{- 7b}x^{2c}$

$= {2}^{a}{\left(3\right)}^{c}\left(\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}\right)x^{a - 7b + 2c}$

Now for term to be independent of $x$, we know

$a - 7b + 2c = 0 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Solving $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$, we get

$b = \dfrac{c + 5}{8}$

Also, $a, b, c \in \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\right\}$

So, $a = 1, b = 1, c = 3$

Therefore, the term independent of $x$ will be

${2}^{1}{\left(3\right)}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{5 !}{1 ! \cdot 1 ! \cdot 3 !} = 1080$
questions.question:

${\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{x^{7}} + 3x^{2}\right)}^{5}$ is _____ .
questions.explanation:
Any term in the expansion of ${\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{x^{7}} + 3x^{2}\right)}^{5}$ is given by

$\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}{\left(2x\right)}^{a}{\left(x^{- 7}\right)}^{b}{\left(3x^{2}\right)}^{c}$

where $a + b + c = 5 . . . \left(i\right)$

$= {2}^{a}{\left(3\right)}^{c}\left(\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}\right)x^{a}x^{- 7b}x^{2c}$

$= {2}^{a}{\left(3\right)}^{c}\left(\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}\right)x^{a - 7b + 2c}$

Now for term to be independent of $x$, we know

$a - 7b + 2c = 0 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Solving $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$, we get

$b = \dfrac{c + 5}{8}$

Also, $a, b, c \in \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\right\}$

So, $a = 1, b = 1, c = 3$

Therefore, the term independent of $x$ will be

${2}^{1}{\left(3\right)}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{5 !}{1 ! \cdot 1 ! \cdot 3 !} = 1080$

questions.q: Let the coefficients of the middle terms in the expansion of \left(\dfrac{1}{6} + \betax\right)4, \left(1 - 3\betax\right)2$ and \left(1 - \dfrac{β}{2}x\right)6, \beta > 0$, respectively form the first three terms of an A.P. If $d$~is the common difference of this A.P., then $50 - \dfrac{2d}{\beta2}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the coefficients of the middle terms in the expansion of \left(\dfrac{1}{6} + \betax\right)4, \left(1 - 3\betax\right)2$ and \left(1 - \dfrac{β}{2}x\right)6, \beta > 0$, respectively form the first three terms of an A.P. If $d$~is the common difference of this A.P., then $50 - \dfrac{2d}{\beta2}$ is equal to _____ .

Given,

Coefficients of middle terms of given expansions \left(\dfrac{1}{6} + \betax\right)4$,~\left(1 - 3\betax\right)2$~and\left(1 - \dfrac{β}{2}x\right)6$~are~$C2 4 \dfrac{1}{6}{β}^{2}, C1 2 \left(- 3\beta\right) \text{ and } C3 6 \left(\dfrac{- \beta}{2}\right)3$~respectively,

Now it is given that middle terms are forming an~$A . P$

So,~$2 C1 2 \left(- 3\beta\right) = C3 6 \left(\dfrac{- \beta}{2}\right)3 + C2 4 \dfrac{1}{6}{β}^{2}$

$⇒ 2 . 2\left(- 3\beta\right) = {β}^{2} - \dfrac{5{β}^{3}}{2}$

$⇒ - 24 = 2\beta - 5{β}^{2}$

$⇒ 5{β}^{2} - 2\beta - 24 = 0$

$⇒ 5{β}^{2} - 12\beta + 10\beta - 24 = 0$

$⇒ \beta\left(5\beta - 12\right) + 2\left(5\beta - 12\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\beta + 2\right)\left(5\beta - 12\right) = 0$

So,~$\beta = \dfrac{12}{5}$~and~$\beta = - 2$~{which is not possible as \beta > 0}$

Now~$d = C1 2 \left(- 3\beta\right) - C2 4 \dfrac{1}{6}{β}^{2} = - 6\beta - {β}^{2}$

Now putting the value of~$\beta \text{ and } d$~in~$50 - \dfrac{2d}{\beta2}$~we get,

$50 - \dfrac{2d}{\beta2} = 50 - 2\left(- 6\beta - {β}^{2}\right){β}^{2} = 50 + \dfrac{12}{β} + 2 = 57$

On solving~$n = 118$~and~$r = 34$

questions.q: If the remainder when $x$ is divided by $4$ is $3$, then the remainder when \left(2020 + x\right)2022$ is divided by $8$ is ___ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$x = 4k + 3$

$∴ \left(2020 + x\right)2022 = \left(2020 + 4k + 3\right)2022$

$= \left(4\left(505 + k\right) + 3\right)2022$

$= \left(4\lambda + 3\right)2022 = \left(16{λ}^{2} + 24\lambda + 9\right)1011$

$= \left(8\left(2{λ}^{2} + 3\lambda + 1\right) + 1\right)1011$

questions.q: Number of integral terms in the expansion of \left\{7\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 11\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right)\right\}824$ is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that,

General term in expansion of \left(( 7{)}^{1 / 2} + ( 11{)}^{1 / 6}\right)824$ is given by,

${t}_{r + 1} = Cr 824 \cdot 7\dfrac{824 - r}{2} \cdot 11\dfrac{r}{6}$

For integral term, $r$ must be multiple of $6$ and should be less than $824$

So, the series will be $r = 0, 6, 12, . . . . . 822$

Now, finding number of terms we get,

$822 = 0 + \left(n - 1\right)6$

$⇒ 137 = \left(n - 1\right)$

$⇒ n = 138$

Hence, total integral terms will be $138$

questions.q: ${50}^{th }$ root of a number $x$ is $12$ and ${50}^{th }$ root of another number $y$ is $18$ . Then the remainder obtained on dividing $( x + y )$ by $25$ is ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$x\dfrac{1}{50} = 12 ⇒ x = {12}^{50}$

$y\dfrac{1}{50} = 18 ⇒ y = {18}^{50}$

So,

$x + y = {12}^{50} + {18}^{50}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + y}{25} = \dfrac{1250}{25} + \dfrac{1850}{25}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + y}{25} = \dfrac{\left({12}^{3}\right)16{12}^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{\left({18}^{2}\right)25}{25}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + y}{25} = \dfrac{\left(1728\right)16{12}^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{\left(325 - 1\right)25}{25}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + y}{25} = \dfrac{\left(1725 + 3\right)16{12}^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{\left(325 - 1\right)25}{25}$

So, remainder is

$\dfrac{{3}^{16}{12}^{2}}{25} - 1 = \dfrac{\left({3}^{3}\right)5 \times 3 \times 144}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(25 + 2\right)5 \times 3 \times 144}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(25 + 2\right)5 \times 3 \times \left(150 - 6\right)}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{{2}^{5} \times 3 \times \left(- 6\right)}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(25 + 7\right) \times 3 \times \left(- 6\right)}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(21\right) \times \left(- 6\right)}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(25 - 4\right) \times \left(- 6\right)}{25} - 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(- 4\right) \times \left(- 6\right)}{25} - 1$

$= 24 - 1 = 23$

Hence, the remainder is~$23$

questions.q: Let the ratio of the fifth term from the beginning to the fifth term from the end in the binomial expansion of \left(24 + \dfrac{1}{34}\right)n$, in the increasing powers of $\dfrac{1}{34}$~be~$64 : 1$. If the sixth term from the beginning is $\dfrac{α}{34}$, then $\alpha$ is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The ratio of the fifth term from the beginning to the fifth term from the end in the binomial expansion of \left(24 + \dfrac{1}{34}\right)n$~in the increasing powers of $\dfrac{1}{34}$~be~$64 : 1$

Now according to given data we have,

$\dfrac{T5}{Tn - 3} = \dfrac{C4 n \left({2}^{1 / 4}\right)n - 4\left({3}^{- 1 / 4}\right)4}{Cn - 4 n \left({2}^{1 / 4}\right)4\left({3}^{- 1 / 4}\right)n - 4} = \dfrac{64}{1}$

$⇒ 2\dfrac{n - 8}{4}3\dfrac{n - 8}{4} = {6}^{1 / 4}$

$⇒ {6}^{n - 8} = 6$

$⇒ n - 8 = 1 ⇒ n = 9$

So,~${T}_{6} = C5 9 \left({2}^{1 / 4}\right)4\left({3}^{- 1 / 4}\right)5 = \dfrac{84}{34}$

Now comparing with~${T}_{6} = \dfrac{α}{34}$,

We get~$\alpha = 84$

$

questions.q: The number of positive integers& $k$ such that the constant term in the binomial expansion of \left(2x^{3} + \dfrac{3}{xk}\right)12, x \ne 0$~is ${2}^{8} \cdot l$, where~$l$ is an odd integer, is ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For& \left(2x^{3} + \dfrac{3}{xk}\right)12$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 12 \left(2x^{3}\right)12 - r \cdot \left(\dfrac{3}{xk}\right)r = Cr 12 \cdot {2}^{12 - r} \cdot {3}^{r} \cdot x^{36 - 3r - kr}$

For the term to be independent of~$x$,

$36 - 3r - kr = 0$~$⇒ r = \dfrac{36}{k + 3}$~

Here~$k$~can be~$0, 1, 3, 6, 9$~for~$r$~to be a whole number.

But for~$Cr 12 \cdot {2}^{12 - r} \cdot {3}^{r}$~to be in the form of~${2}^{8} \cdot l$

Only $k = 3, 6$ satisfies the above relation.

$

questions.q: If the constant term in the binomial expansion of \left(\dfrac{x\dfrac{5}{2}}{2} - \dfrac{4}{xl}\right)9$ is $- 84$ and the coefficient of $x^{- 3l}$ is ${2}^{α}\beta$ where $\beta < 0$ is an odd number, then \left|\alphal - \beta\right|$ is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The constant term in the binomial expansion of \left(\dfrac{x\dfrac{5}{2}}{2} - \dfrac{4}{xl}\right)9$ is $- 84$ and the coefficient of $x^{- 3}$ is ${2}^{α}\beta$

Now General Term of the binomial is given by,~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 9 \left(\dfrac{x\dfrac{5}{2}}{2}\right)9 - r\left(\dfrac{- 4}{xl}\right)r = \left(- 1\right)r{C}_{r}x^{\dfrac{45}{2} - \dfrac{5r}{2} - lr}{2}^{3 - 9}$

Now for constant term $45 - 5r - 2lr = 0 ⇒ r = \dfrac{45}{5 + 2l}$

So, coefficient of constant term will be,

\left(- 1\right)9{×}^{9}{C}_{r}{2}^{3r - 9} = - 84 ⇒ r = 3$

Now putting the value of~$r$~in~$r = \dfrac{45}{5 + 2l}$~we get,~$l = 5$

Now coefficient of $x^{- 3l} = x^{- 15} ⇒ \dfrac{45}{2} - \dfrac{5r}{2} - lr = - 15 ⇒ r = 5$ when $l = 5$
Now coefficient of $x^{- 15} = \left(-1\right)59{C}_{5}{2}^{6} = - 63 \left({2}^{7}\right) = \beta\left({2}^{α}\right)

Hence, on comparing we get,~\alpha =$7, $\beta = -$63 & l = 5$

So, the value of \left|\alphal - \beta\right| = \left|$7 $\times$5 - \left(-$63\right)\right| = 98$

questions.q: Let for the& ${9}^{th}$~term in the binomial expansion of~\left(3 + 6x\right)n$, in the increasing powers of~$6x$, to be the greatest for~$x = \dfrac{3}{2}$, the least value of~$n$~is~${n}_{0}$. If~$k$~is the ratio of the coefficient of~$x^{6}$~to the coefficient of~$x^{3}$, then~$k + {n}_{0}$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,&

\left(3 + 6x\right)n = {3}^{n}\left(1 + 2x\right)n$

Now if~${T}_{9}$~is numerically greatest term, then~${T}_{8} \le {T}_{9} \ge {T}_{10}$

So,~$C7 n {3}^{n - 7}\left(6x\right)7 \le C8 n {3}^{n - 8}\left(6x\right)8 \ge C9 n {3}^{n - 9}\left(6x\right)9$

$⇒ \dfrac{n !}{\left(n - 7\right) ! 7 !}9 \le \dfrac{n !}{\left(n - 8\right) ! 8 !}3 \cdot \left(6x\right) \ge \dfrac{n !}{\left(n - 9\right) ! 9 !}\left(6x\right)2$

$⇒ \mathop{9\left(n - 7\right)\left(n - 8\right)}_{⏟} \le \mathop{\dfrac{18\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}{ \left(n - 8\right)8} \ge $\dfrac{36}{9 . 8}\dfrac{9}{4}}_{⏟}$

$⇒ 72 ≤ 27\left(n - 7\right)$~and~$27 ≥ 9 \left(n - 8\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{29}{3} \len$~and~$n ≤ 11$

So,~${n}_{0} = 10$

For~\left(3 + 6x\right)10$

Now~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 10 {3}^{10 - r}\left(6x\right)r$

For coefficient~of~$x^{6}$

$r = 6 ⇒ C6 10 {3}^{4} \cdot {6}^{6}$

For coefficient~of~$x^{3}$

$r = 3 ⇒ C3 10 {3}^{7} \cdot {6}^{3}$

So,~$k = \dfrac{C6 10}{C3 10} \cdot \dfrac{{3}^{4} \cdot {6}^{6}}{{3}^{7} \cdot {6}^{3}} = \dfrac{10 ! 7 ! 3 !}{6 ! 4 ! 10 !} \cdot8$

$⇒ k = 14$

$∴ k + {n}_{0} = 24
